messages:
incident-bot: Pager: HIGH - KV prefix cache hit-rate collapse for tenant aurelia-bank in enterprise-vpc-eu-west1. Alerts: increased latency, token cost spike, 502s on model-route /v1/generate. Please acknowledge and triage.

alex (oncall-sre): acked. I'm on it. seeing a drop from ~92% to ~8% hit-rate on prefix cache for tenant prefix `aurelia-*`. Traffic surge? or cache pollution?

jamie (sre-lead): thx alex. quick ask: can you confirm if this is confined to tenant namespace or cross-tenant? also any KV eviction logs?

alex (oncall-sre): checking kv metrics now. eviction rate spiked at 10:12 UTC. keys churn high for prefix `aurelia-` and there's a lot of long-tail prefixes being written. looks like a consumption pattern change from customer side (batch prefetch turned on?)

lin (eng-runtime): pinged. if it's cache pollution, short-term option: disable tenant prefix caching for that tenant and fallback to global cache + direct runtime path. that'll increase latency a little but restore correctness. I can run the mitigation script.

alex (oncall-sre): agree. Sophia, can you reach out to AureliaBank ops to ask if they flipped any client setting? we should let them know we're doing a mitigation.

sophia (customer-ops): on it. I'll message their infra lead. ETA 10min. telling them we may disable tenant cache temporarily.

lin (eng-runtime): mitigation steps (pre-approved playbook):

```
# disable tenant prefix cache for tenant id 7231
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  https://controlplane.redwood/api/v1/tenants/7231/cache-config \
  -d '{"prefix_cache_enabled": false, "reason":"inc-1963207777 - hitrate collapse"}'

# confirm change
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" https://controlplane.redwood/api/v1/tenants/7231/cache-config
```

lin (eng-runtime): I'll hold on executing until alex gives +1 to avoid race with autoscaler / config sync.

alex (oncall-sre): go for it. execute and post responses. I'll monitor KV hit-rate and request latencies.

deploy-bot: config-update: tenant/7231/prefix-cache set to false by lin at 1963208110. Rollout: immediate.

lin (eng-runtime): done. API returned 200. cache-config shows prefix_cache_enabled: false.

alex (oncall-sre): metrics: hit-rate creeping back up to ~55% since we disabled tenant prefix caching (global fallback + direct runtime caches helping). 502s dropping. latency median up ~30ms but p95 better.

jamie (sre-lead): good. next: we need to confirm isolation — ensure no other tenants affected by this config change and check eviction/backfill IO. alex, run a quick query for other tenants with high eviction at same interval.

alex (oncall-sre): running. results: no other tenant had the same spike. looks isolated to tenant 7231.

sophia (customer-ops): AureliaBank responded: they recently toggled a client-side aggressive prefetch flag in their SDK rollout at 09:58 UTC. They didn't realize it created high cardinality prefixes. They're rolling back now. They appreciate quick mitigation.

jamie (sre-lead): ok, plan: keep tenant prefix cache disabled for 1 hour while customer backfills and we monitor. follow-up actions: (1) add temporary rate limit on large prefix writes for that tenant, (2) schedule a post-incident meeting with eng-runtime + customer integration to add better server-side protections, (3) add a monitoring alert for prefix entropy spikes.

lin (eng-runtime): I'll open a PR for server-side guardrails (reject writes that create >N new prefixes/min for enterprise-tenants) and add a canary release. Also suggestion: auto-disable tenant prefix cache if eviction rate > threshold for X minutes.

alex (oncall-sre): handing off to next oncall: maya. I'm going offline in ~20m, leaving monitoring dashboards open and playbook steps documented below.

maya (next-oncall): taking over. thanks alex — I'll watch for regressions and follow through on jamie's tasks. please add any runbook links.

alex (oncall-sre): runbook snippets:
- Playbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/kv-prefix-cache-pollution
- Mitigation script: https://redwood.internal/tools/cache-admin
- Query used: `SELECT tenant_id, eviction_rate, prefix_entropy FROM kv_metrics WHERE ts > now() - interval '30 minutes' ORDER BY eviction_rate DESC;`

jamie (sre-lead): notes for postmortem: initial classification: cache pollution due to customer-side prefetch rollout. Impact: degraded latency for AureliaBank traffic only, transient 502s (~3.4% of their requests during spike window), cost increase estimated +12% for the hour. Mitigation: disabled tenant prefix cache, customer rollback.

sophia (customer-ops): AureliaBank wants a short incident summary and confirmation when we re-enable. I'll prepare comms and coordinate re-enable testing window with them.

maya (next-oncall): will keep tenant cache disabled and prepare to re-enable after customer confirms rollback and we validate prefix entropy < threshold for 30m. I'll also create a short post-incident task list in ops.

incident-bot: Incident 1963207777 status: acknowledged -> mitigated (tenant cache disabled). Owner: alex -> maya (handoff). Severity: high -> downgraded to medium as errors subsided.

jamie (sre-lead): closing notes: add follow-ups to the 1-week SRE backlog: automated detect-and-disable, write quota for prefix churn, customer integration checklist.

sophia (customer-ops): AureliaBank confirmed rollback at 1963212000. please coordinate re-enable window with them; prefer low-traffic window tomorrow 02:00 UTC.

maya (next-oncall): noted. I'll schedule re-enable for 02:00 UTC tomorrow, monitor 30m after re-enable, and keep Sophia looped in.

alex (oncall-sre): thanks team. logging final metrics and closing my shift.

jamie (sre-lead): thanks everyone. put initial blameless summary in incidents doc and assign owners for PRs.

sophia (customer-ops): I'll send the customer summary and coordinate the re-enable test. :white_check_mark:
